boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Kansas

cards.title: Tacos El King
cards.subtitle: 61 23rd St at Louisiana, Lawrence
cards.notes: Check the current day’s posted closing time before leaving; this location lists evening service and late-night hours for pickup or food runs.

cards.evidence_claim: Tacos El King lists Lawrence hours until 2 a.m. Monday–Thursday and 2:30 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Mon–Thu 4 p.m.–2 a.m.; Fri–Sat 4 p.m.–2:30 a.m. Confirm before going.

cards.title: Hawaiian Bros Island Grill
cards.subtitle: 1501 W. 23rd St, Lawrence

cards.title: Domino's on Iowa Street

cards.title: Domino's on West 23rd

cards.short_summary: A second late-listed Domino’s destination on West 23rd Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino’s official 832 Iowa Street page lists its nearby 1008 W. 23rd Street Lawrence location as open until 1 a.m.
cards.source_title: Domino's Pizza at 832 Iowa Street — nearby locations
cards.access_notes: The official nearby-locations listing displayed “Open Today Until 1:00 AM” for 1008 W. 23rd St; verify before ordering.

cards.title: Taco Bell on West 6th
cards.subtitle: 1220 W. 6th St, Lawrence

cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday at 1220 W. 6th Street.
cards.access_notes: Listed drive-thru hours: 2 a.m. Sun–Thu and 3 a.m. Fri–Sat; dine-in closes earlier. Confirm before going.

cards.title: Taco Bell at 1408 West 23rd

cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists 1408 W. 23rd Street drive-thru hours until midnight Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and until 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Taco Bell at Bauer Farm
cards.subtitle: 4721 Bauer Farm Dr, Lawrence
cards.notes: Check the store page immediately before a drive-thru run, especially on weekends when its official listing shows a later closing time.
cards.short_summary: A northwest Lawrence option with drive-thru hours extending into early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru service at 4721 Bauer Farm Drive until 1 a.m. most days and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 4721 Bauer Farm Drive, Lawrence
cards.access_notes: Listed drive-thru hours: 1 a.m. Sun–Thu and 2 a.m. Fri–Sat; dine-in closes earlier. Confirm before going.

cards.title: Wendy's on West 23rd
cards.subtitle: 523 W. 23rd St, Lawrence
cards.notes: Use the location page to check current conditions and choose restaurant or drive-thru service; both are currently listed through midnight every day.
cards.short_summary: An all-week, midnight-listed fast-food stop on West 23rd Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists both restaurant and drive-thru hours from 8 a.m. to midnight daily at 523 W. 23rd Street.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists restaurant and drive-thru hours until 12 a.m. daily. Verify the day’s hours before travel.

cards.title: Papa Johns on Mississippi Street
cards.subtitle: 918 Mississippi St, Lawrence
cards.notes: Order carryout or delivery through the official store page and confirm the live close; listed hours are later on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A pizza pickup or delivery option with 2 a.m. daily and 3 a.m. weekend listings.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns lists carryout and delivery until 2 a.m. daily and until 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday at 918 Mississippi Street.
cards.source_title: Papa Johns Pizza — Mississippi Street, Lawrence
cards.access_notes: Listed carryout and delivery hours: 2 a.m. Sun–Thu and 3 a.m. Fri–Sat. Confirm before ordering.

cards.title: Jimmy John's on Massachusetts Street
cards.subtitle: 922 Massachusetts St, Lawrence
cards.notes: Use the operator’s location page to confirm the day and place an order; late hours are listed specifically for Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A downtown sandwich destination whose official listing reaches 2 a.m. on weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Jimmy John’s lists store and delivery hours until 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday at 922 Massachusetts Street.
cards.access_notes: Listed store and delivery hours: until 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday; 10 p.m. Sunday–Thursday. Verify before going.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented KU spaces for quiet work, group projects, creative production, research, and campus connection.

cards.title: Watson Library
cards.subtitle: 1425 Jayhawk Blvd. • library study hub
cards.notes: Start on the third floor for group tables, computers, FitDesks, carrels, and Studio K; move upstairs when your task needs a quieter setting.
cards.short_summary: A central library building with distinct study setups across three upper floors.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries identifies Watson as a location with group and quiet study areas, computer workstations, scanners, printers, and reservable study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Check KU Libraries’ current hours before going; study rooms support academic study and research.

cards.entity_name: Watson Library Fifth Floor Study Space
cards.title: Watson’s Fifth-Floor Study Space
cards.subtitle: Watson Library • quiet individual work
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing that benefits from low noise; the fifth floor combines quiet individual study with International Collections and a reflection room.
cards.short_summary: A named quiet-study floor inside Watson Library.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries lists quiet individual study space, International Collections, and a reflection room on Watson Library’s fifth floor.
cards.access_notes: Conversation and phone use are not permitted in Watson’s designated quiet-study areas, including the fifth floor.

cards.title: Studio K
cards.subtitle: Watson Library third floor • quick recording studio
cards.notes: Use this named room when a class presentation or demonstration needs recording; reserve it with the video equipment purpose in mind.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in recording studio for speeches, demonstrations, and presentations.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries describes Studio K as a quick-record studio where users can record a speech, demonstration, or presentation shortly after arriving.
cards.access_notes: Priority use goes to KU students, staff, or faculty using the room’s video-recording equipment.

cards.title: Anschutz Library
cards.subtitle: KU Libraries • study, support, and technology
cards.notes: Choose Anschutz for a project needing research help, writing support, tutoring, or computer access; check the floor map before meeting a group.
cards.short_summary: A library building that concentrates academic support, technology, and varied study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries says Anschutz hosts research, writing, and technology help, tutoring, collaboration spaces, and study areas.
cards.access_notes: Open computer areas on the third and fourth floors contain more than 100 workstations.

cards.title: David Beaham Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Anschutz Library fourth floor • quiet study
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor when you need a named quiet room for solo reading or writing; keep the space suited to focused, low-noise work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet room in Anschutz Library.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries identifies the David Beaham Reading Room as a quiet study room on the east portion of Anschutz Library’s fourth floor.
cards.access_notes: Quiet areas are set aside for reading, solo computer work, and other quiet tasks.

cards.title: Anschutz Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Anschutz Library second floor • creative work
cards.notes: Reserve time for a hands-on project, podcasting, or 3D-printing exploration; beginners and curious makers are explicitly welcomed by KU Libraries.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor creative space for making, recording, and collaborative experimentation.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries describes the Anschutz Makerspace as a second-floor space with tools for 3D printing, podcasting, and creative discovery.
cards.access_notes: The floor map lists the Makerspace on Anschutz Library’s second floor; confirm reservation procedures with KU Libraries.

cards.title: Anschutz Reflection Room
cards.subtitle: Anschutz Library third floor • reflection space
cards.notes: Use this separate room for quiet reflection or prayer, respecting people of all faiths, spiritual beliefs, and practices while you share the space.
cards.short_summary: A named third-floor space for peaceful reflection within Anschutz Library.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries’ floor map lists a Reflection Room on the third floor of Anschutz Library.
cards.access_notes: KU Libraries asks users of reflection spaces to practice tolerance of all faiths, spiritual beliefs, and practices.

cards.title: Spahr Engineering Library
cards.subtitle: LEEP2 • individual and collaborative study
cards.notes: Use Spahr for engineering-focused work with collaborators, then reserve a group room through your KU email or Engineering Student Success if needed.
cards.short_summary: An engineering-library setting with individual, collaborative, and group-study options.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries says Spahr Engineering Library includes individual and collaborative study spaces, group study rooms, and desktop workstations.
cards.access_notes: Desktop computer access is limited to KU School of Engineering affiliates; group rooms can be reserved through KU email or Engineering Student Success.

cards.title: Murphy Art & Architecture Library
cards.subtitle: Spencer Museum of Art, Level 1 • research library
cards.notes: Pair a museum-area visit with on-site research in this named library; use the collections there when art, design, architecture, or planning work needs sources.
cards.short_summary: An art and architecture research library located in the Spencer Museum of Art.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries identifies Murphy Art & Architecture Library in the Spencer Museum of Art and states it is open to any on-site user.
cards.access_notes: The library is open to on-site users; borrowing privileges and use rules vary by material.

cards.title: Marilyn Stokstad Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Kenneth Spencer Research Library • primary-source research
cards.notes: Create an Aeon account and request materials before working with special collections; check in at the third-floor reception desk when you arrive.
cards.short_summary: A special-collections reading room for working with Spencer Research Library materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenneth Spencer Research Library provides research services in the Marilyn Stokstad Reading Room and requires an Aeon account for on-site collection access.
cards.source_title: Use Collections | Kenneth Spencer Research Library
cards.access_notes: No appointment is necessary to use collections, but researchers must have a current Aeon account and follow Reading Room policies.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten free, under-21-friendly places for a low-key meet-up on campus or nearby in Lawrence.

cards.title: Look through the galleries together
cards.subtitle: Spencer Museum of Art · KU campus
cards.notes: Meet at the entrance, choose a floor, and take turns pointing out one work that starts a conversation. Check the museum’s posted gallery hours before leaving.
cards.short_summary: Two floors of art galleries make an easy, self-paced indoor hang.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spencer Museum states that admission is free for all visitors, always.
cards.access_notes: Open hours and gallery closures are posted on the museum’s visit page; no admission purchase is required.

cards.title: Browse local history exhibits
cards.subtitle: Watkins Museum of History · 1047 Massachusetts St.
cards.notes: Start with a gallery that catches the group’s eye, then compare the local stories or objects each person noticed. Confirm current museum hours before your visit.
cards.short_summary: A downtown history museum for an unhurried, conversation-friendly stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Watkins Museum of History lists admission as free.
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Tuesday–Saturday public hours; admission does not require a purchase.

cards.title: Spread out for a park-side chat
cards.subtitle: South Park · downtown Lawrence
cards.notes: Bring your own blanket or use open lawn space for a conversation, sketches, or a quiet reset. Stay in general public areas and respect any reserved space.
cards.short_summary: A downtown public-park setting for a simple outdoor meet-up.
cards.evidence_claim: South Park is listed as a Lawrence community park; Kansas law states no charge may be made for park entrance or use of park facilities.
cards.access_notes: Lawrence says its public parks are open daily from 6 a.m. to 11:30 p.m.; avoid any separately reservable area.

cards.title: Take a river-adjacent walk
cards.subtitle: Burcham Park · Lawrence community park
cards.notes: Use the paths for an easy walking conversation, then pause somewhere out of the way to plan the rest of the day. Follow posted park rules and conditions.
cards.short_summary: A named community park for a no-cost walking hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Burcham Park is listed as a Lawrence community park; Kansas law states no charge may be made for park entrance or use of park facilities.
cards.access_notes: Lawrence identifies Burcham as a community park; use general public areas rather than reservable facilities.

cards.title: Meet for an outdoor reset
cards.subtitle: Buford M. Watson, Jr. Park · Lawrence community park
cards.notes: Pick a visible public spot for a short catch-up, a book swap, or a walk. Keep the plan flexible around weather and any posted maintenance notices.
cards.short_summary: A city community park suited to a casual daylight meet-up.
cards.evidence_claim: Buford M. Watson, Jr. Park is listed as a Lawrence community park; Kansas law states no charge may be made for park entrance or use of park facilities.
cards.access_notes: Lawrence identifies this as a community park; use ordinary public access, not a reserved event area.

cards.title: Walk a lap and catch up
cards.subtitle: Centennial Park · Lawrence community park
cards.notes: Set an easy walking pace and let everyone choose a topic for the lap. Use the shared public grounds respectfully and yield space to other park users.
cards.short_summary: A community-park walk that needs no ticket or purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: Centennial Park is listed as a Lawrence community park; Kansas law states no charge may be made for park entrance or use of park facilities.
cards.access_notes: Lawrence identifies Centennial as a community park; reservable shelters or event spaces may have separate rules.

cards.title: Get outside for a group walk
cards.subtitle: Clinton Lake Outlet Park · Lawrence community park
cards.notes: Choose a daytime route that fits the group, keep to established public areas, and take a few minutes to notice the landscape. Check conditions before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A named public park for a no-spend outdoor break.
cards.evidence_claim: Clinton Lake Outlet Park is listed as a Lawrence community park; Kansas law states no charge may be made for park entrance or use of park facilities.
cards.access_notes: Lawrence lists the outlet park among its community parks; use public areas and follow posted safety guidance.

cards.title: Pause by the riverfront
cards.subtitle: Riverfront Park · Lawrence community park
cards.notes: Use the public park setting for a short walk, a photo challenge, or a relaxed conversation. Stay with your group and observe all trail and park signage.
cards.short_summary: A city-managed riverfront setting for a free daytime hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Riverfront Park is listed as a Lawrence community park; Kansas law states no charge may be made for park entrance or use of park facilities.
cards.access_notes: Lawrence lists Riverfront Park as a community park; use normal public access rather than any reservable facility.

cards.title: Take a low-key nature break
cards.subtitle: Prairie Park · Lawrence community park
cards.notes: Meet for a gentle walk and let the group set the pace. Keep to public paths and leave plants, wildlife, and shared spaces undisturbed for the next visitors.
cards.short_summary: A city community park for a quiet, no-cost outdoor pause.
cards.evidence_claim: Prairie Park is listed as a Lawrence community park; Kansas law states no charge may be made for park entrance or use of park facilities.
cards.access_notes: Lawrence identifies Prairie Park as a community park; follow posted rules and use general public areas.

cards.title: Make a simple meetup outdoors
cards.subtitle: Holcom Park · Lawrence community park
cards.notes: Use open public space for a walk-and-talk or a shared study break before heading back to campus. Check posted notices and avoid any booked facility area.
cards.short_summary: A Lawrence community park for an easy, free group reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Holcom Park is listed as a Lawrence community park; Kansas law states no charge may be made for park entrance or use of park facilities.
cards.access_notes: Lawrence lists Holcom Park among its community parks; general park access is separate from reservable facilities.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For

cards.entity_name: Watson Library Third Floor Study Space
cards.title: Watson Library Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Watson Library • 1425 Jayhawk Blvd.
cards.notes: Set up here when your work needs a computer workstation, study carrel, or FitDesk; reservable study rooms and Studio K are also on this floor.

cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries identifies Watson’s third floor as having group study space, computer workstations, FitDesks, silent study in the stacks, and reservable study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Use during Watson Library open hours. Study rooms require an online reservation; quiet-designated areas follow the library noise policy.

cards.entity_name: Watson Library Fourth Floor Study Space
cards.title: Watson Library Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: Watson Library • 1425 Jayhawk Blvd.
cards.notes: Choose this floor for individual or small-group reading and writing; keep conversations out of the designated quiet areas and use lower-volume group space.
cards.short_summary: Quiet individual and group study space on Watson’s fourth floor.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries lists quiet individual and group study space and silent study in the stacks on Watson Library’s fourth floor.
cards.access_notes: Use during Watson Library open hours. KU Libraries designates Watson fourth-floor quiet-study areas; conversation and phone use are not permitted there.

cards.entity_name: Watson Library Fifth Floor Study Space
cards.title: Watson Library Fifth Floor
cards.subtitle: Watson Library • 1425 Jayhawk Blvd.
cards.notes: Bring reading, drafting, or other solo work to the fifth floor, where quiet study sits alongside International Collections and Gothic-window views.
cards.short_summary: A quiet Watson study floor with International Collections nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries identifies Watson’s fifth floor as quiet individual study space and notes its International Collections and Gothic-window views.

cards.title: Studio K
cards.subtitle: Watson Library, Third Floor
cards.notes: Reserve this production-ready room when a class presentation, speech, or demonstration needs a quick recording; confirm availability before arriving.

cards.entity_name: Anschutz Library Second Floor Quiet Study
cards.title: Anschutz Library Second Floor
cards.subtitle: Anschutz Library • 1301 Hoch Auditoria Dr.
cards.notes: Use the second floor for solo reading or laptop work when you need a quieter setting; bring headphones and keep calls for designated cell zones.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study space in KU’s Anschutz Library.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries states that Anschutz Library’s second floor has quiet study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Use during Anschutz Library open hours. Quiet-study areas do not permit conversation or phone use under the KU Libraries noise policy.

cards.entity_name: Anschutz Library Third Floor Group Study Space
cards.title: Anschutz Library Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Anschutz Library • 1301 Hoch Auditoria Dr.
cards.notes: Bring a project team here for work near computer workstations, printing, and scanning; reserve a room if your group needs a closed-door setup.
cards.short_summary: A group-work floor with computers, printing, and scanning.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries says Anschutz’s third floor has group study spaces, computer workstations, printing, and scanning.
cards.access_notes: Use during Anschutz Library open hours. Group study is allowed outside designated quiet areas; reservable rooms have separate booking rules.

cards.title: David Beaham Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Anschutz Library, Fourth Floor
cards.notes: Choose this named reading room for concentrated reading and solo computer work; use a carrel or table and keep the room quiet for others.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet reading room with tables, carrels, power, and wireless access.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries identifies the David Beaham Reading Room on Anschutz’s fourth floor as a quiet study room for reading and solo computer work, with carrels, tables, power outlets, and wireless access.
cards.access_notes: Located on the east portion of Anschutz’s fourth floor; use during library open hours and follow quiet-study expectations.

cards.entity_name: Murphy Art & Architecture Library Study Rooms
cards.title: Murphy Art & Architecture Library
cards.subtitle: Level 1, Spencer Museum of Art • 1301 Mississippi St.
cards.notes: Reserve a study room for coursework while working near art, architecture, design, and urban-planning collections; verify the current library schedule first.
cards.short_summary: Reservable academic study rooms within KU’s art and architecture library.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries states that study rooms at the Murphy Art & Architecture Library are available to support academic study and research.
cards.source_title: Murphy Art & Architecture Library | KU Libraries
cards.access_notes: The library is on the first level of the Spencer Museum of Art. KU Libraries says it is open to any on-site user; confirm current hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Joe and Joyce Hale Media Center
cards.title: Joe and Joyce Hale Media Center
cards.subtitle: Gorton Music & Dance Library, Murphy Hall Room 240
cards.notes: Use a media workstation for digital score editing, audio, or video work; ask at circulation for in-library headphones or MIDI keyboards.
cards.short_summary: A KU-patron media workspace with Windows PCs, Macs, and in-library equipment checkout.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries says the Joe and Joyce Hale Media Center has eight Windows PCs and two Macs, with software including Sibelius, MuseScore, GarageBand, and Xcode.
cards.source_title: Music and Dance Library Media Facilities | KU Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located in the Gorton Music & Dance Library. The media-center computers are for KU patrons; headphones and MIDI keyboards are available at the circulation desk.

cards.title: Spahr Engineering Library
cards.subtitle: LEEP2 • 1536 W. 15th St.
cards.notes: Use this LEEP2 library for individual or collaborative engineering coursework; book a group room through KU email or contact Engineering Student Success.
cards.short_summary: Engineering-library study space with group rooms and affiliate desktop workstations.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Libraries states that Spahr Engineering Library includes individual and collaborative study spaces, group study rooms, and desktop computer workstations for School of Engineering affiliates.
cards.access_notes: Located in LEEP2. Reserve group rooms through a KU email account or the Engineering Student Success office; desktop-computer access is limited to Engineering affiliates.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on campus-adjacent downtown Lawrence corridors, each with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: See Douglas County history at Watkins
cards.subtitle: 1047 Massachusetts Street — Mass Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk to the former city hall at 1047 Massachusetts Street and explore its history galleries during the museum’s posted Tuesday–Saturday hours.
cards.short_summary: A free downtown history museum in the former city hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Watkins Museum lists free admission, its 1047 Massachusetts Street location, and Tuesday–Saturday hours.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; posted hours are Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.

cards.title: Take the gazebo-and-gardens loop
cards.subtitle: 1141 Massachusetts Street — Mass Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the paths around the William Kelly Bandstand, Roosevelt Fountain, flower gardens, and Butterfly Garden; bring a picnic or a sketchbook.
cards.short_summary: A historic city park split across Massachusetts Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies South Park at 1141 Massachusetts Street and lists its bandstand, fountain, gardens, playground, and picnic tables.
cards.source_title: South Park – City of Lawrence, Kansas
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park; check City notices and event schedules before visiting.

cards.title: Check the galleries and arts calendar

cards.title: Use the downtown library as a reset stop

cards.title: Browse records and music media

cards.title: Browse handmade art across two floors

cards.evidence_claim: Phoenix Gallery lists its downtown location at 825 Massachusetts Street and says visitors can browse two floors of art.

cards.title: Find a toy-store stop in the 900 block

cards.title: Browse the 800-block antique mall

cards.title: Plan an outdoor-gear browse

cards.title: Browse instruments in the 1300 block

cards.access_notes: Retail destination; verify current hours with the business.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Kansas traditions, from Mount Oread ceremony to Jayhawk game-day rituals.

cards.title: Join the Rock Chalk Chant
cards.subtitle: University-wide yell rooted in Mount Oread limestone
cards.notes: Listen for the slow chant at a KU event, then join the repeated “Rock Chalk, Jayhawk, KU” cadence with the crowd.
cards.short_summary: KU’s signature cheer began as a student yell in the 1880s.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Athletics states that Rock Chalk was adopted as the college yell in 1886 and was known as the school’s official yell by fall 1887.
cards.access_notes: Participation depends on the event; follow venue and event guidance.

cards.title: Wave the Wheat
cards.subtitle: Synchronized arm-waving at KU sporting events
cards.notes: At the appropriate game moment, raise both arms and move them side to side with the crowd to evoke a wheat field.
cards.short_summary: A sea of waving arms turns KU crowds into a field-of-wheat visual.
cards.evidence_claim: KU describes Waving the Wheat as a tradition in which a large group waves hands side to side, resembling wheat in the wind.
cards.source_title: Wave the Wheat Wall | KU Memorial Unions
cards.access_notes: Use the gesture at designated moments during sporting events.

cards.title: Walk Down the Hill at Commencement
cards.subtitle: Graduates’ ceremonial descent from Mount Oread
cards.notes: If graduating, follow the commencement procession from Memorial Drive through the Campanile and onward to Memorial Stadium.
cards.short_summary: KU frames the graduate walk down Mount Oread as commencement’s centerpiece.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Commencement calls the ceremonial walk down Mount Oread its most treasured tradition and says it begins on Memorial Drive.
cards.access_notes: For graduating students participating in KU Commencement; consult the current ceremony instructions.

cards.title: Save the Campanile Passage for Graduation
cards.subtitle: Memorial Campanile, Mount Oread
cards.notes: Treat the Campanile passage as part of the graduation milestone: KU notes that superstitious students avoid it until Commencement.
cards.short_summary: The commencement route gives a campus superstition a ceremonial payoff.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Commencement says superstitious students avoid marching through Memorial Campanile until Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Respect the site and use public routes; the ceremonial passage is part of Commencement.

cards.title: Wear Crimson and Blue
cards.subtitle: KU’s official athletic colors
cards.notes: Use crimson and blue when showing KU spirit at campus gatherings or athletics events; KU traces their official athletic adoption to 1896.
cards.short_summary: The color pairing is a long-running visual marker of KU identity.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Athletics states that the KU Athletic Board adopted crimson and blue as the university’s official team colors in May 1896.
cards.access_notes: Personal attire is optional; comply with any event-specific policies.

cards.title: Learn “I’m a Jayhawk”
cards.subtitle: KU fight song associated with athletics traditions
cards.notes: Follow the band or crowd at an event and learn the fight song by listening first; its history is documented by Kansas Athletics.
cards.short_summary: A 1912 song that became popular with KU students in 1920.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Athletics says “I’m a Jayhawk,” written in 1912 by KU graduate George Bowles, became popular with KU students in 1920.
cards.access_notes: Participation depends on the event; follow band and venue guidance.

cards.entity_name: The Crimson and the Blue Alma Mater
cards.title: Sing “The Crimson and the Blue”
cards.subtitle: KU’s alma mater
cards.notes: At a tradition-focused gathering, listen for the alma mater and join only if you know the words; KU commonly pairs it with Rock Chalk.
cards.short_summary: KU’s alma mater predates many current campus rituals.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Memorial Unions states that KU’s alma mater, “The Crimson and the Blue,” was written in 1891 and is usually followed by the Rock Chalk Chant.
cards.access_notes: Participation depends on the event; follow the event program and performers.

cards.title: Spot Big Jay
cards.subtitle: KU’s 3-D Jayhawk mascot
cards.notes: Look for Big Jay at a KU athletics or spirit event and enjoy the mascot’s role in the school’s Jayhawk visual tradition.
cards.short_summary: Big Jay brought the Jayhawk from illustration into mascot form.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Athletics states that the KU Alumni Association provided a Jayhawk mascot costume in the 1960s, introducing Big Jay.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances vary by event; do not enter restricted performance areas.

cards.title: Remember Baby Jay’s Homecoming Debut
cards.subtitle: 1971 halftime Jayhawk-mascot milestone
cards.notes: Use a KU traditions display or athletics history page to see the origin story: Baby Jay was introduced from a huge egg at Homecoming.
cards.short_summary: A halftime reveal added Baby Jay to KU’s mascot family.
cards.evidence_claim: KU Athletics reports that fans saw Big Jay’s companion, Baby Jay, hatch from a huge egg at 1971 Homecoming halftime.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; current Homecoming programming may differ.

cards.title: Start Hawk Week at Traditions Night
cards.subtitle: Memorial Stadium welcome-week tradition session
cards.notes: Attend the listed Hawk Week session to learn KU traditions in Memorial Stadium; check the current schedule and any participation instructions.
cards.short_summary: A fall welcome-week event explicitly devoted to KU traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: KU’s Hawk Week page lists Traditions Night and describes it as an opportunity to catch Jayhawk spirit and learn KU traditions.
cards.source_title: Hawk Week | KU Center for Orientation & Transition Programs
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for Hawk Week; confirm date, location, accessibility details, and requirements on the current page.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Kansas, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm, under-21-safe first-weekend route through KU landmarks, public exhibits, and student-centered spaces.

cards.title: Start with the Jayhawk Welcome Center
cards.subtitle: Orientation stop · 1266 Oread Avenue
cards.notes: Begin by using the interactive exhibits to connect campus history and programs to the places you will encounter on the hill.
cards.short_summary: Get a visual introduction to KU before setting out across Mount Oread.
cards.evidence_claim: KU identifies the Jayhawk Welcome Center at 1266 Oread Ave. and says it has interactive exhibits about KU history and programs.
cards.access_notes: Campus-visit availability varies; the admissions page directs visitors to check current visit options.

cards.title: Pause at the Memorial Campanile
cards.subtitle: Campus landmark · 1450 Memorial Drive
cards.notes: Walk up to the memorial room and take a moment with the World War II names before continuing along Memorial Drive.
cards.short_summary: A 120-foot limestone memorial with a 53-bell carillon.
cards.evidence_claim: The Memorial Campanile was dedicated in 1951; its memorial room lists 277 KU community members who died in World War II, and its carillon has 53 bells.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; carillon concerts are performed by university and guest artists.

cards.title: Follow Memorial Drive’s curve
cards.subtitle: Scenic walk · above Marvin Grove and Potter Lake
cards.notes: Use this W-shaped drive as your walking link between the Campanile, memorials, and the north-campus landscape below.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped ridge-route designed around KU’s World War II memorial.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Drive was designed to complement the Memorial Campanile and follows the crest of Mount Oread above Marvin Grove and Potter Lake.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route on the Lawrence campus; follow posted campus conditions and accessibility routes.

cards.title: Take the long way past Potter Lake
cards.subtitle: North-campus landscape · Mount Oread
cards.notes: Circle the lake on foot, then keep the stop to the banks and paths; plan a study break rather than any water activity.
cards.short_summary: A two-acre campus lake originally built as a fire-water reservoir.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says Potter Lake was constructed in 1910 as a reservoir, is now a storm-water retention pond, and prohibits swimming.
cards.access_notes: Swimming is prohibited; boating is permitted only for classes and academic research, and state fishing laws apply.

cards.title: Step into the Spencer Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Gallery visit · 1301 Mississippi Street
cards.notes: Choose one gallery or current exhibition to explore slowly, then use the museum’s visitor guidance to plan the rest of your visit.
cards.short_summary: A free KU art museum with public galleries and validated garage parking.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spencer Museum of Art states that admission is free for all visitors and lists regular gallery hours, including weekend afternoon hours.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours: Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Thursday until 8 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; closures are listed by the museum.

cards.title: Meet the Panorama at the Natural History Museum
cards.subtitle: Dyche Hall · 1345 Jayhawk Boulevard
cards.notes: Make the four-floor exhibit visit your main indoor stop, beginning with the Panorama and then following the displays that interest you.
cards.short_summary: A natural-history museum in Dyche Hall with the Panorama, fossils, and live-animal exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says the Natural History Museum has four floors of public exhibits, including the historic Panorama, fossils, live snakes, and insects.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday noon–4 p.m.; closed Mondays. Admission is a suggested contribution, while KU students are free.

cards.title: Regroup at the Kansas Union
cards.subtitle: Community stop · 1301 Jayhawk Boulevard
cards.notes: Use the building as a practical reset: look for current programming, find a shared table, or browse its historical displays across the levels.
cards.short_summary: KU’s historic community center for events, dining, student programming, and displays.
cards.evidence_claim: KU describes the Kansas Union as a campus destination and says Student Union Activities plans more than 200 events each year for the Jayhawk community.
cards.access_notes: The Union lists building hours separately and notes that hours and access can change, including during renovations or breaks.

cards.title: Choose a seat at Watson Library
cards.subtitle: Study stop · 1425 Jayhawk Boulevard
cards.notes: Find either a group or quiet area, then try a small task such as reserving a study room or asking a librarian one question.
cards.short_summary: KU’s oldest and largest library, with quiet and group study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says Watson Library, built in 1924, is its oldest and largest library and offers group and quiet study areas, workstations, scanners, and printers.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms support academic study and research; check the library’s current hours and room-reservation availability before going.

cards.title: See basketball’s original rules at DeBruce
cards.subtitle: History stop · 1647 Naismith Drive
cards.notes: Look for the original Rules of Basket Ball and the Naismith statue outside, then use the adjoining student-center spaces as a breather.
cards.short_summary: A KU student center adjoining Allen Fieldhouse and housing Naismith’s original rules.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says the DeBruce Center houses James Naismith’s original Rules of Basket Ball and includes student-center amenities and meeting rooms.
cards.access_notes: The building is connected to Allen Fieldhouse; the Union publishes current operating hours and notes game-related closures.

cards.title: Finish with a low-pressure Rec orientation
cards.subtitle: Active reset · 1740 Watkins Center Drive
cards.notes: Bring your KUID, check in at the Welcome Center, and take a first lap through the track, courts, and equipment areas at your pace.
cards.short_summary: A KU recreation facility with fitness equipment, courts, a track, climbing wall, and table games.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says Ambler SRFC has cardiovascular and resistance equipment, courts, studios, a walking/jogging track, climbing wall, table tennis, and Teqball.
cards.access_notes: Controlled-access facility for authorized KU community users; eligible participants must present valid KU or ASRFC photo ID at entry.
